subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency

Hi Olaf/Hannah 

Thanks again for hopping on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can draft a mutual action plan: 

1) Recap of needs from the call
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer PII and transaction logs.
- Secondary need: Low-latency access for APAC customers (read-only/edge requests)  looking to understand tolerable cross-region routing vs local processing.
- Preference expressed: Private VPC if feasible; exploring Dedicated GPU pools as an intermediate option if timelines/costs are prohibitive.

2) Clarifying questions
- Do you need ALL inference traffic to remain in EU for regulatory reasons, or just data-at-rest (e.g., logging, analytics)?
- Expected peak QPS (or tokens/sec) and average daily request volume  helps us size Dedicated vs Private.
- Are there specific encryption/KMS requirements (customer-managed keys / HSM)?

I've attached a short product comparison that outlines Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private from a deployment-timeline and responsibility standpoint  see product-compare.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa + Dev: technical deep dive to go over network/topology and timelines
- Olaf/Hannah: share the residency checklist or the internal compliance doc you mentioned (SOC 2 scope, cross-border rules)
- I'll draft a mutual action plan and estimated timelines/pricing for Dedicated and Private by end of week once we have the QPS numbers.

Thanks  appreciate the clarity you shared today.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Olaf Berg <olaf.berg@nordbank.eu>

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the recap  that's accurate. A couple notes to clarify on our side: 

- Residency: For regulated accounts we need ALL customer data (inference inputs, logs, and derived embeddings) to persist in the EU. In-flight routing for inference is acceptable if the model execution hosts are also in the EU; in other words we cannot have primary model execution or logging in non-EU regions for EU accounts.
- APAC latency: We have a set of business customers in APAC who expect <200ms median latency. If cross-region routing from APAC users to EU inference would breach SLAs for those accounts, we will need regional handling (edge routing or local Dedicated capacity in APAC).
- Compliance artifacts: I'll attach our residency checklist (nordbank-residency-requirements.docx).

We are leaning toward Private VPC because it gives our security/compliance team the most confidence, but we need to see realistic timelines and pricing for Private vs Dedicated (and understand the contractual language around data residency and cross-region fallback).

Olaf
Head of Cloud Architecture | NordBank
olaf.berg@nordbank.eu

Attachment: nordbank-residency-requirements.docx

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency

Hi all 

Thanks, Olaf  that doc is helpful. A few technical clarifications / options so you have a concrete picture: 

Summary of deployment options (short):
- Hosted (EU region): We can guarantee that primary model execution and logs remain in an EU region (e.g., eu-west1). Hosted customers can opt into regional-only routing and contractual residency clauses. Good for fast time-to-value; SOC 2 + encryption in transit/rest standard.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in EU): Dedicated GPU pools deployed into an EU region provide predictable throughput and isolated capacity. Logs and storage can be configured to remain in-EU. Typical lead time for capacity alignment and testing: 2–4 weeks after PO.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer-managed network connectors (VPC peering, PrivateLink) and optional on-prem install. Full control of network egress and KMS (customer-managed keys/HSM). Security review + provisioning: typically 6–10 weeks depending on network changes and audit scope.

Cross-region routing and APAC latency:
- If NordBank requires sub-200ms median for APAC, we recommend either (a) Dedicated APAC pool for APAC customers, or (b) an edge routing strategy with local frontends + EU model execution where acceptable. Our smart routing supports policy-level routing (region, customer tier).

Encryption & keys:
- We support customer-managed KMS keys for data-at-rest and for signing. HSM integrations are available for Private deployments.

Attachments & refs:
- deployment-options-matrix.xlsx attached (timelines, responsibilities, rough cost bands)
- internal region guide: https://redwood.example.com/regions-deployment
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NB-2026-042

A couple of asks to size things: 
1) Target peak QPS or tokens/sec (per region)
2) Expected retention/replication needs for logs/embeddings (e.g., 30 days, 90 days)

Happy to jump on a technical call this week with your infra/security folks.
—Dev
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
